trust_decision.summary: A LightGlue checkpoint's nested keypoint-detector config must never reach remote-code resolution: the checkpoint's own trust_remote_code flag drives AutoConfig.from_pretrained at the config post-init and is forwarded into AutoModelForKeypointDetection.from_config at model init, so the published fix deletes the flag from the config dataclass and from both call sites (in the modular source and both generated files) and adds mlinter rule TRF014 to keep it out of native integrations.

landing_point.why: It is the only place in the tree where data from a checkpoint's config.json is turned into a remote-code resolution (AutoConfig.from_pretrained fed untrusted _name_or_path plus the config's own trust_remote_code); a reader of 'RCE in the LightGlue model loading path' greps trust_remote_code in this package and lands here first, one hop from the model __init__ the summary names.

fix_sites.entry_point: same as configuration_lightglue.py:76-92, via the modular source of truth
same as modeling_lightglue.py:503-507, via the modular source of truth

fix_sites.module_kind: new linter rule module, outside src/transformers

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The model-init line only forwards a caller override into AutoModelForKeypointDetection, whose mapping contains nothing but SuperPoint (src/transformers/models/auto/modeling_auto.py:1738-1742), so it looks unable to load anything remote and the real control is assumed to be the config's AutoConfig call; separately, the config code says the flag exists on purpose (configuration_lightglue.py:76-79).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The plain SuperPoint nested-dict path must keep working: a keypoint_detector_config dict with no model_type defaults to superpoint, is built through CONFIG_MAPPING with attn_implementation='eager', and the default LightGlueConfig() builds a SuperPointConfig. Every lightglue test builds its config exactly this way (tests/models/lightglue/test_modeling_lightglue.py:44-93), so a fix that rejects nested dicts or any _name_or_path/auto_map key outright, or forces one detector class, breaks model construction everywhere.

O6_input_shapes: nested keypoint_detector_config dict with no model_type (defaults to superpoint) -> local CONFIG_MAPPING branch
nested dict with an unregistered model_type and _name_or_path -> AutoConfig.from_pretrained(trust_remote_code=...) at the config stage

nested dict with a registered model_type that also carries auto_map{'AutoModelForKeypointDetection': '<repo>--<Class>'} -> remote model class still loaded at model init, because auto_map beats the local mapping once the flag is explicitly True
keypoint_detector_config already a PreTrainedConfig object (not a dict) carrying auto_map -> dict branch skipped, flag still forwarded at model init
trust_remote_code supplied inside the checkpoint's own config.json rather than by the caller
mlinter rule shapes: foo(trust_remote_code=...), foo(**{'trust_remote_code': ...}), foo(**dict(trust_remote_code=...)); a bare **kwargs variable is deliberately not covered

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the identical nested-dict -> config branch, plus a trust_remote_code field and an AutoConfig.from_pretrained fallback for unregistered detector types
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SuperGlue is the sibling keypoint-matching integration and its __post_init__ is a near-copy of LightGlue's; a maintainer adding 'detectors other than SuperPoint, e.g. DISK' would naturally write the same fallback here.
same one-line composition wrapper already calling the same auto factory; the LightGlue model init is the obvious template to copy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new loader branch added to the modular source silently reappears in both generated files (configuration_lightglue.py and modeling_lightglue.py)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the repo's modular/generated pipeline means the source of truth and the shipped copy are two implementations of the same code by construction, so a maintainer can edit one and believe it is done.

O9_family: untrusted-control-sphere code inclusion leading to remote code execution (CWE-829): a model-config field steers AutoConfig/AutoModel remote-code resolution

O10_build.toolchain: pip install -e . (setup.py); torch required to build the LightGlue model; rich + tomllib for utils/mlinter
O10_build.project_tests: tests/models/lightglue/test_modeling_lightglue.py:37-136 (tiny SuperPoint sub-config, CPU); tests/models/superglue/test_modeling_superglue.py:37-90 (sibling integration); tests/repo_utils/test_mlinter.py:34-600 (per-rule analyze_file tests, the pattern a TRF014 test would follow)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Hardcode trust_remote_code=False (or pop the kwarg) in the AutoConfig.from_pretrained call in __post_init__, keep the config field, and leave the model-init pass-through, stopping there.

out_of_scope_notes: src/transformers/cli/download.py:35-40 and src/transformers/cli/serve.py:578-580,2157-2186 expose trust_remote_code as an explicit user CLI flag; that is a user opt-in, not config-driven, so it is outside this advisory's property and was not pursued.
